  could not calculate 'dbar'; using detector spacing
3: In secr.fit(capthist = combinedCH, CL = TRUE, details = list(telemetrysigma = TRUE),  :
  'secr.fit' failed because initial values not found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'
> 

Do you see any problems with my coding? I have tried different buffer sizes, with/without a mask, details$telemetrybvn = TRUE, and the same errors arise. 

Starting values of D = log(0.01), g0 = log(100) to log(100000), and sigma=log(300) to log(10000) don't help.

Any suggestions for starting values to try?  Deer density is about 0.07 deer/ha, home range size is about 300 ha.

Thanks,

Duane

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Combining telemetry and DNA capture
parts:
Hi Duane

Sorry for the delay - as you know, this went in the 'too hard' pile for a few days. I know that weakly documented implementation of combined telemetry & SECR is temperamental, and I thought you might be a hapless victim, but perhaps the problem is more basic.

Your code looks impeccable except possibly for the starting values for which you didn't show the code (obviously you should specify lambda0 not  g0 for detectfn = 'HHN', which is definitely the detectfn to use).

It must be a worry that there are no DNA recaptures (as I read the summary) and no overlap between the telemetry animals and the DNA sample. That seems to mean that you have a 'no recapture' dataset overall, hence no means to estimate lambda0 and D.

For the telemetered animals you will get an estimate of the pooled sigma essentially without error just by applying RPSV(telemCH, CC=TRUE) to the telemetry part of the dataset. That can be used as a fixed input for analysing the DNA histories (fixed = list(sigma = XXX)) but without recaptures I don't see that lambda0 is going to be identifiable.

Murray
